info.title: Petstore (demo)
info.summary: A demo pet store you can actually call from this page.
info.description:
Fake pet store API used as the ApiGlow demo playground. Based on the official [Swagger Petstore](https://petstore3.swagger.io) schema, enriched with extra auth schemes (bearer, basic, OAuth2 authorization code + client credentials) and named examples to exercise every try-it feature.

The server is **same-origin and answered in the browser** by a service worker (`demo/mock-sw.js`): every operation below really runs — create a pet, order it, read it back — with no backend, no CORS and no proxy. The data lives in the worker's memory and resets when the browser recycles it. Credentials are never verified — except by the **Failure showcase** tag, whose `/failures/protected` endpoint really enforces the demo bearer token.

The OAuth2 flows run against the same worker (`/demo-api/oauth/`), consent page included: all four flows really answer, wherever the demo is hosted. Two top-level `webhooks` (OpenAPI 3.1) and the callbacks of `POST /pet/{petId}/subscribe` are declarative only — no delivery is ever sent; they exist to exercise the webhook simulator and the callbacks section. The schema is written in OpenAPI **3.2** and showcases its novelties — `query` and `additionalOperations` methods, `querystring` parameters, sequential media types (`itemSchema`), response `summary`, tag hierarchy, named servers, deprecated security schemes and the device authorization flow.

servers.name: demo
servers.description: Same-origin demo API, answered in the browser by `demo/mock-sw.js`. Relative on purpose: the doc resolves it against its own URL, so the demo works on whatever host and port serves it.

tags.name: stream
tags.description: Streaming endpoints, declared as a child of `pet` via the OpenAPI 3.2 tag hierarchy (`parent`). The demo mock streams three status changes and then closes the connection.

tags.name: errors
tags.description: Endpoints that exist to demonstrate how this documentation renders failure: server errors, throttling, auth walls, validation, latency and broken payloads. Each one really produces what it declares.

Multiple tags can be provided with comma separated strings. Use tag1, tag2, tag3 for testing.

**Deprecated**: use `QUERY /pet/search` instead, which filters on tags and status at once and takes its criteria in a body. This endpoint is removed in the next major version.

get.summary: Filter pets with a raw query string.
get.description: OpenAPI 3.2 — the whole query string is described by a single parameter `in: querystring`, instead of individual `name=value` pairs. Made for filter languages (RSQL, JSONPath, GraphQL…) whose syntax does not survive being split into pairs, nor being re-encoded. The demo mock understands a small RSQL subset: `field==value`, `field!=value` and `field=in=(a,b)`, joined by `;`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: RSQL expression, sent verbatim as the query string.

query.summary: Search pets with a structured body.
query.description: OpenAPI 3.2 — `query` joins `get`, `post`… as a Path Item field: a safe and idempotent read that carries a request body, which `GET` cannot describe. The examples use the new `dataValue` (structured) and `serializedValue` (already-serialized string) fields, which replace the ambiguous `value`.

compact.description: A `serializedValue` is a string in the wire format of the media type — no re-encoding is applied to it.

get.description: OpenAPI 3.2 — sequential media types: `itemSchema` describes **one item** of the stream (one SSE event, one JSON line), where `schema` would have to describe the whole, endless body. This response also shows the other 3.2 relaxation: `description` is now optional on a response, `summary` alone is enough.

get.description: Unconditionally answers **500** with the standard `Error` body — what an unhandled server-side crash looks like in this documentation.
Unconditionally answers **503 Service Unavailable** carrying a `Retry-After` header — watch the response panel count it down.

503.description: Deliberately unavailable; the header says when to come back.

get.description: Answers **429 Too Many Requests**: this endpoint's quota is permanently exhausted, `RateLimit-Remaining` is `0`, and `Retry-After` says when the window resets.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window: zero, here.

get.description: Answers **200** only with the demo bearer token (`auth.bearerAuth` in the prefilled environment); anything else gets a **401** — the first place the prefilled credentials visibly matter.

message.description: Confirmation that the token was accepted.

get.description: Even a valid demo token gets a **403** here: authentication is not authorization, and this endpoint's scope is granted to nobody.

401.description: No valid bearer token at all.

403.description: Authenticated, but this scope is granted to nobody.

post.description: Validates the body: a well-formed payload answers **200**, anything else a **422** whose body lists each rejected field with a JSON Pointer.

requestBody.description: The payload to validate: a well-formed email and a positive quantity.

422.description: The payload is invalid; `errors[]` says why, field by field.

get.description: A deliberately slow **200** (~4 s): long enough for the send meter and `Server-Timing` to become legible, short enough to wait for.
Answers **200** with `Content-Type: application/json` and a truncated body that is not valid JSON — the response view falls back to showing the raw bytes.

200.description: Malformed on purpose: the declared JSON never parses.

get.summary: A host that does not resolve
get.description: This operation pins its own server on a `.invalid` host — a TLD RFC 2606 guarantees will never resolve. Sending shows the "unreachable" network diagnosis, distinct from a CORS refusal.

200.description: Never arrives: the host does not resolve.

get.summary: A server that never says CORS
get.description: This operation pins its own server on a reachable public origin that sends no CORS headers: the browser blocks the read, and the panel diagnoses a CORS refusal — not an unreachable host.

200.description: The server answers, but the browser refuses to show it to this origin.

get.description: The server accepts the request and never responds. The Cancel control next to Send is how you get out.

200.description: Never produced: the request stays in flight until you cancel it.

post.description:
Sent to the URL you registered whenever a pet you follow changes status.

Answer `200` within 5 seconds: the payload is retried with exponential backoff for 24 hours otherwise. Answer `410` to have the subscription dropped.

parameters.name: X-Petstore-Signature

parameters.name: X-Petstore-Delivery
parameters.description: Id of this delivery attempt. Stable across retries of the same event.

200.description: Delivery acknowledged. The body is ignored.

410.description: Endpoint gone: the subscription is dropped and no further event is sent.

type.description: A stable machine-readable kind for this failure.

ValidationError.description: A 422 body: the request was readable but its content is invalid, field by field.

code.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body.

message.description: Human-readable summary of what was rejected.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the rejected value in the request body.

errors.message: must be a valid email address

petstore_auth.description: OAuth2 against the demo’s own same-origin authorization server, served by the mock service worker — all four flows really answer, anywhere the demo is hosted. Declares its authorization server metadata URL and a device flow, both new in OpenAPI 3.2.

api_key.name: api_key
api_key.description: Legacy header key, kept for existing integrations. Marked `deprecated`, a security scheme field added in OpenAPI 3.2 — use `bearerAuth` instead.

bearerAuth.description: JWT sent as `Authorization: Bearer …`. The demo mock never verifies it: paste anything, or leave it empty and the call still goes through.
